message.content:
**Explicit in the instructions:** The role is “a hedge-fund analyst” keeping a record “on a name you cover.” The instructions do not name that company.

**My inference:** I understood the name being covered to be **NN, Inc. (NNBR)**, not NVIDIA. The source repeatedly centers NN: its title is “Why NN (NNBR) Is Up 24.7%”; it says “To own NN”; and it discusses NN’s pivot, business target, forecasts, valuation, debt, and risks. The record also identifies **NN, Inc.** as the original source of the announcement. NVIDIA appears as the company whose AI data-center racks the cooling production is for, not as the apparent subject of the investment analysis.

Two alternatives I considered and rejected:

1. **That the covered company was NVIDIA.** The source mentions “NVIDIA AI data center racks” and a bigger “NVIDIA centric footprint,” but the article’s title and investment discussion are about NN. Treating NVIDIA as the covered name would be an inference from the customer/program context rather than the source’s central subject.

2. **That the expansion already represented realized revenue or a confirmed direct purchase commitment by NVIDIA.** The source says NN was “targeting US$80–US$90 million of accretive new business in 2026,” and that the capacity was “pre-sold and tied to multi-year, multi-product awards.” Those are reported announcement/target statements; they do not establish realized revenue, and the text does not say NVIDIA itself is the contracting buyer.
